nodes.text: Careful with the door — the wards dislike drafts. Come in. You have questions; everyone who climbs this far does. I keep answers, theories, and one very patient enchanting table.

choices.text: Why do runes burn brighter up here?
What do you make of the Riftgate below?
I'll leave you to the wards.

nodes.text: Four theories: thinner air, older stone, the starfall vein singing through the bedrock, or — my favorite — that altitude is simply *closer to where the runes are from*. Every enchanter who works a season up here brews stronger and burns brighter. The mountain participates. On what terms, I am still negotiating.

choices.text: Teach me. What do you sell?

nodes.text: Eleven years of petitions. I could feel the Riftgate through eighty feet of rock — a hum in a key I almost recognize, and *almost* is everything in my work. Now the way is open, the hum is louder, and my sleep files complaints. I was right to ask. I check that conclusion nightly, the way you check a lock.

The Masons found it already standing when they first cut the deep galleries — older than the city, older than the guild, patient as bedrock. Keys turn there and places answer; the deep folk treat it as furniture, which is the healthiest possible attitude. I treat it as a colleague whose references I am still checking.
Mind the wards on your way out. They remember everyone, and they gossip.
Scrolls of the craft, and dust to practice with. The runes charge nothing extra this high — that part the mountain gives away.
